title: Objective stress rates (Jaumann, Truesdell, Green-Naghdi)
objective: Implement the three objective stress rates required by rate-form constitutive models and provide the corresponding material-tangent conversions (C_IJKL → c^Jau, c^Tru, c^GN) used by the UL tangent emitter.

plan_assets.asset_description: B1.4 objective-rate table with formulas for Jaumann, Truesdell, and Green-Naghdi.

scope: Add `mechdsl.symbolic.objective_rates` module with three functions: `jaumann_tangent(C4, sigma)`, `truesdell_tangent(C4, sigma)`, `green_naghdi_tangent(C4, sigma, R)`.
Each function takes a 4th-order material tangent in the reference configuration and returns the corresponding spatial tangent (3,3,3,3).
Verify via a rigid rotation test: at zero strain, the Cauchy stress rate under each objective rate must vanish.
implementation_steps: Read 07-CONVENTIONS.md for the project's sign convention and Voigt ordering before deriving formulas.
Implement Jaumann first (the default for metals, used by P1-4 by default).
Add Truesdell and Green-Naghdi as follow-ups.
Write a unit test that generates a rigid rotation over 180 degrees and verifies the Cauchy stress rate vanishes under each rate.
Write a unit test on a known simple shear and compare against the hand-calculated tangent.
acceptance_criteria: All three rates implemented as pure functions operating on NumPy arrays.
Rigid rotation test passes for all three rates.
Simple shear comparison passes for Jaumann (the primary path used by P1-4).
verification_commands: uv run pytest packages/mechdsl-core/tests/ -m 'not slow and not gpu' -q

cases: Jaumann tangent at rigid rotation gives zero Cauchy rate
Truesdell tangent at rigid rotation gives zero Cauchy rate
Green-Naghdi tangent at rigid rotation gives zero Cauchy rate
Jaumann tangent on simple shear matches hand calculation

risks: The Green-Naghdi rate requires the polar decomposition F = R U. At near-identity F the rotation R is ill-conditioned. Mitigation: use scipy.linalg.polar and add a conditioning guard.

commands.command: uv run pytest packages/mechdsl-core/tests/ -m 'not slow and not gpu'

completion_notes: Added mechdsl/symbolic/objective_rates.py with two API layers: direct rate functions (jaumann_rate, truesdell_rate, green_naghdi_rate) and spatial tangent conversions (jaumann_tangent, truesdell_tangent, green_naghdi_tangent).

Direct rate functions added beyond stated scope because the rigid-rotation invariance test is mathematically meaningless at the tangent level (D = 0 under rigid rotation => any c:D is trivially zero). The scaffold test names `*_tangent_at_rigid_rotation_*` are preserved but their bodies call the rate functions. Logged as Gate B m1; explicitly documented in the module-level 'Out-of-scope additions' marker section as of follow-up commit 70ca2b7.

truesdell_tangent supports the full Piola push-forward c_ijkl = (1/J) F_iI F_jJ F_kK F_lL C_IJKL via an optional F parameter (default None = identity for Plan A back-compat). Implementation is a single 4-leg einsum. The sigma argument is kept via `del sigma` for API symmetry so downstream callers can branch on rate name without knowing which tangent is being used. jaumann_tangent and green_naghdi_tangent forward F through to truesdell_tangent.

jaumann_tangent adds the Prandtl-Reuss correction T(sigma); the correction itself is configuration-independent (sigma is already spatial), so jaumann_tangent = truesdell_tangent(F) + T(sigma) at any F.

green_naghdi_tangent raises NotImplementedError if R != I — fail-fast seam for the future large-rotation push-forward where the polar-decomposition spin diverges from the continuum spin. Aligned with ir.md rejection rule.
Simple shear test verifies the Prandtl-Reuss identity at both the rank-4 level (c_Jau - c_Tru == T(sigma)) and the rank-2 level (c_Jau : D matches 2*mu*D + D@sigma + sigma@D for simple shear).

Full-F push-forward test (test_truesdell_tangent_full_f_simple_shear_matches_b_formula) uses an analytical simplification c_ijkl = mu*(B_ik*B_jl + B_il*B_jk) computed via a different einsum string than the source code, providing an independent validation of the 4-leg push-forward end-to-end. Spot-checked components against pure hand calculation (c_1212 = 1.5, c_1111 = 3.125, c_1122 = 0.5).
All docstrings use ASCII math notation (sigma, Omega, delta, lam, mu) matching the convention in symbolic/models/j2_power_law.py. Ruff RUF002 is enabled repo-wide.
Follow-up gate cycle (2026-04-16, commit 70ca2b7): closed Gate B m2 (deferred full-F push-forward). Review score 8 -> 9. m1 (out-of-scope rate functions) preserved with explicit module-level marker.
